# Accordions (/components/accordions)





## Frequently asked [#frequently-asked]

<Accordions type="single">
  <Accordion title="Why am I getting 429 responses?">
    Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Which endpoints accept an idempotency key?">
    | Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
    | ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
    | `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
    | `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
    | `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I retry safely from TypeScript?">
    ```ts
    import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

    const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

    export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
      try {
        const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
          const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
          return listAvailablePets(limit);
        }
        throw error;
      }
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What is the difference between code and message?">
    Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Several open at once [#several-open-at-once]

<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="A section that starts closed">
    The Petstore API exposes pets, store orders and user accounts over HTTPS. Every request is authenticated, every response is JSON, and every list endpoint is paginated. This page walks through the parts of that contract you are most likely to need on your first integration, and points at the reference pages for the rest.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A section with a very long title that will need to wrap on a narrow viewport because it keeps going">
    Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key. Send the same key with a retried request and the API returns the original response rather than performing the operation twice. Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours, which is long enough to cover a retry queue draining after an outage but short enough that keys can be recycled.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Authentication [#authentication]

The Petstore API exposes pets, store orders and user accounts over HTTPS. Every request is authenticated, every response is JSON, and every list endpoint is paginated. This page walks through the parts of that contract you are most likely to need on your first integration, and points at the reference pages for the rest.

## Rate limits [#rate-limits]

Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.

## Errors [#errors]

Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.


# Callouts (/components/callouts)



Callouts come from the default component set, so they need no import.

## The four types [#the-four-types]

<Callout type="info">
  An informational callout. Use it for context a reader can skip.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn" title="Rate limits apply">
  A warning callout with an explicit title. Use it for something that will bite later.
</Callout>

<Callout type="error" title="Breaking change in v3.3">
  An error callout. `GET /user/login` is removed in v3.3. Move to `POST /auth/token` before upgrading.
</Callout>

<Callout>
  A callout with no type at all, which should fall back to the default styling.
</Callout>

## A callout holding real content [#a-callout-holding-real-content]

<Callout type="warn" title="Read this before enabling retries">
  Retrying a non-idempotent request can create duplicate orders. Before you turn on
  automatic retries, check that every endpoint you call accepts an idempotency key:

  | Endpoint            | Idempotent | Key header        |
  | ------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
  | `POST /pet`         | Yes        | `Idempotency-Key` |
  | `POST /store/order` | Yes        | `Idempotency-Key` |
  | `DELETE /pet/petId` | No         | not accepted      |

  The SDKs send the header for you when you pass `idempotencyKey` to the call.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="Example">
  The TypeScript SDK reads `Retry-After` and backs off without any configuration:

  ```ts
  import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

  const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

  export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
    try {
      const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
      return result;
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
        const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
        return listAvailablePets(limit);
      }
      throw error;
    }
  }
  ```

  Set `maxRetries: 0` in `ClientOptions` if you would rather handle it yourself.
</Callout>

Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.

## Callouts in sequence [#callouts-in-sequence]

<Callout type="info">
  First of three consecutive callouts, to check vertical rhythm.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn">
  Second of three.
</Callout>

<Callout type="error">
  Third of three.
</Callout>

Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key. Send the same key with a retried request and the API returns the original response rather than performing the operation twice. Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours, which is long enough to cover a retry queue draining after an outage but short enough that keys can be recycled.

# Code blocks (/components/code-blocks)



## One block per language [#one-block-per-language]

```ts
import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
  try {
    const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
      const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
      return listAvailablePets(limit);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

```python
import os
from petstore_sdk import SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiException

client = SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(api_key=os.environ["PETSTORE_API_KEY"])

def list_available_pets(limit: int = 100):
    try:
        return client.pet.find_pets_by_status(status="available", limit=limit)
    except ApiException as exc:
        if exc.status_code == 429:
            raise RuntimeError("rate limited; let the SDK retry policy handle this") from exc
        raise
```

```csharp
using Acme.Petstore.Sdk;

var client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(
    apiKey: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("PETSTORE_API_KEY"));

var pets = await client.PetController.FindPetsByStatusAsync(status: "available", limit: 100);
```

## A line far wider than the page [#a-line-far-wider-than-the-page]

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.petstore.example.com/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available&limit=100&offset=0&sort=name&order=ascending&include=category,tags,photoUrls" -H "api_key: $PETSTORE_API_KEY" -H "Accept: application/json" --compressed --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 --max-time 30
```

## A block with no language [#a-block-with-no-language]

```
GET /v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available HTTP/1.1
Host: api.petstore.example.com
api_key: ****************************
Accept: application/json
```

## A long response body [#a-long-response-body]

```json
{
  "pets": [
    { "id": 1, "name": "Kitty", "status": "available", "category": { "id": 1, "name": "Cats" }, "tags": [{ "id": 1, "name": "indoor" }] },
    { "id": 2, "name": "Rex", "status": "pending", "category": { "id": 2, "name": "Dogs" }, "tags": [{ "id": 2, "name": "large" }, { "id": 3, "name": "trained" }] },
    { "id": 3, "name": "Whiskers", "status": "sold", "category": { "id": 1, "name": "Cats" }, "tags": [] }
  ],
  "nextCursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMCwibGltaXQiOjEwMH0",
  "total": 1284
}
```

## Inline code of unusual length [#inline-code-of-unusual-length]

A parameter named `includeCategoryAndTagsAndPhotoUrlsInTheResponsePayload` inside a sentence,
followed by a bare URL that cannot break: [https://api.petstore.example.com/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available\&limit=100\&offset=0\&sort=name\&order=ascending\&include=category,tags,photoUrls](https://api.petstore.example.com/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available\&limit=100\&offset=0\&sort=name\&order=ascending\&include=category,tags,photoUrls)

Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.

# Components (/components)



The Petstore API exposes pets, store orders and user accounts over HTTPS. Every request is authenticated, every response is JSON, and every list endpoint is paginated. This page walks through the parts of that contract you are most likely to need on your first integration, and points at the reference pages for the rest.

<Callout type="info" title="How to read these pages">
  Each page below uses one component family, with enough content on it to show how the
  component behaves when it is full rather than when it holds one line.
</Callout>

  <Card title="Callouts" href="/components/callouts" description="info, warn and error, including callouts that hold lists and code" />

Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.

## A second diagram, as a fenced block [#a-second-diagram-as-a-fenced-block]

Some Markdown toolchains render a `mermaid` fence instead of a component.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant API
    participant Store
    Client->>API: POST /pet
    API->>Store: persist
    Store-->>API: id
    API-->>Client: 201 Created
```

Anything below this line should still render, whichever way the two diagrams above resolve.


# Steps (/components/steps)





## Integrating the SDK [#integrating-the-sdk]

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Create an API key [#create-an-api-key]

    Open the dashboard, create a key scoped to the environment you are integrating, and store it
    outside your source tree. The examples below read it from `PETSTORE_API_KEY`.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Install the package [#install-the-package]

    ```bash
    curl -X GET "https://api.petstore.example.com/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available&limit=100&offset=0&sort=name&order=ascending&include=category,tags,photoUrls" -H "api_key: $PETSTORE_API_KEY" -H "Accept: application/json" --compressed --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 --max-time 30
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Construct one client [#construct-one-client]

    Construct the client once and reuse it. It owns a connection pool, and building one per request
    exhausts sockets under load.

    ```ts
    import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

    const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

    export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
      try {
        const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
          const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
          return listAvailablePets(limit);
        }
        throw error;
      }
    }
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Handle rate limits [#handle-rate-limits]

    Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Go to production [#go-to-production]

    | Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
    | ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
    | `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
    | `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
    | `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
    | `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |
  </Step>
</Steps>

Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key. Send the same key with a retried request and the API returns the original response rather than performing the operation twice. Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours, which is long enough to cover a retry queue draining after an outage but short enough that keys can be recycled.

## Three tabs, one per language [#three-tabs-one-per-language]

<Tabs items="['TypeScript', 'Python', 'C#']">
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```ts
    import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

    const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

    export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
      try {
        const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
          const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
          return listAvailablePets(limit);
        }
        throw error;
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    from petstore_sdk import SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiException

    client = SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(api_key=os.environ["PETSTORE_API_KEY"])

    def list_available_pets(limit: int = 100):
        try:
            return client.pet.find_pets_by_status(status="available", limit=limit)
        except ApiException as exc:
            if exc.status_code == 429:
                raise RuntimeError("rate limited; let the SDK retry policy handle this") from exc
            raise
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="C#">
    ```csharp

        apiKey: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("PETSTORE_API_KEY"));

    var pets = await client.PetController.FindPetsByStatusAsync(status: "available", limit: 100);
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.

## More tabs than fit on a narrow screen [#more-tabs-than-fit-on-a-narrow-screen]

<Tabs items="['TypeScript', 'Python', 'C#', 'Java', 'PHP', 'Ruby', 'Go', 'curl', 'HTTPie', 'PowerShell']">
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    The tab strip should scroll or wrap rather than overflow the page.

# Twoslash (/components/twoslash)



Twoslash needs `fumadocs-twoslash` and a Shiki transformer wired into `mdxOptions`. This page
uses twoslash syntax with none of that in place, to see whether the markers render as hover
type information or leak into the page as literal comments.

## The full example [#the-full-example]

````ts twoslash lineNumbers
type Player = {
  /**
   * The player name
   * ```php
   * $a = "60"
   * ```
   *
   * @default 'user'
   */
  name: string;
};

/**
 * A custom function.
 *
 * @example
 *
 * ```ts
 * const str = fn("hello world")
 * console.log(str)
 * ```
 */
function fn<const T extends string>(s: T): T {
  return s;
}

// ---cut---
// @noErrors
console.g;
//       ^|

const player: Player = { name: 'Hello World' };
//    ^?

fn('test');
````

## A minimal twoslash block [#a-minimal-twoslash-block]

```ts twoslash
const greeting = "hello";
//    ^?
```

## The same code with no twoslash flag [#the-same-code-with-no-twoslash-flag]

```ts
const greeting = "hello";
```

Anything below this line should still render, whichever way the blocks above resolve.

## ClientOptions [#clientoptions]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  apiKey: {
    description: 'The API key sent as the api_key header on every request.',
    type: 'string',
    default: 'undefined',
  },
  timeout: {
    description: 'Per-attempt timeout in milliseconds. Applies to each retry, not to the call as a whole.',
    type: 'number',
    default: '30000',
  },
  maxRetries: {
    description: 'How many times a failed request is retried before the error is thrown.',
    type: 'number',
    default: '3',
  },
  environment: {
    description: 'Which declared server the client talks to.',
    type: '&#x22;production&#x22; | &#x22;staging&#x22;',
    default: '&#x22;production&#x22;',
  },
  fetch: {
    description: 'A replacement fetch implementation, used as the seam in tests.',
    type: 'typeof fetch',
    default: 'globalThis.fetch',
  },
}"
/>


# Typography (/components/typography)



The Petstore API exposes pets, store orders and user accounts over HTTPS. Every request is authenticated, every response is JSON, and every list endpoint is paginated. This page walks through the parts of that contract you are most likely to need on your first integration, and points at the reference pages for the rest.

## Heading level two [#heading-level-two]

Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.

### Heading level three [#heading-level-three]

Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.

#### Heading level four [#heading-level-four]

Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key. Send the same key with a retried request and the API returns the original response rather than performing the operation twice. Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours, which is long enough to cover a retry queue draining after an outage but short enough that keys can be recycled.

##### Heading level five [#heading-level-five]

A fifth-level heading, which most themes stop styling distinctly.

###### Heading level six [#heading-level-six]

A sixth-level heading.

## A table wider than the page [#a-table-wider-than-the-page]

| Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
| `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
| `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |

## A deeply nested list [#a-deeply-nested-list]

1. Create an API key in the dashboard and store it outside your source tree.
2. Install the SDK for your language from its public registry.
   * TypeScript from npm
   * Python from PyPI
   * C# from NuGet
3. Construct one client and reuse it for the lifetime of your process.
   * The client owns a connection pool
   * Constructing one per request exhausts sockets under load
     * On Linux you will see `EADDRNOTAVAIL` first
     * On Windows the symptom is a slow creep in handle count
4. Make your first call against a read-only endpoint to confirm credentials.
5. Add error handling for `429` and `5xx` before you go to production.

## A blockquote [#a-blockquote]

> Pets created through the API are visible to every user in your organisation
> immediately. There is no draft state, and no soft delete: a `DELETE` removes
> the record and its photo attachments in the same transaction.

## Overflow stress [#overflow-stress]

A bare unbreakable URL in a paragraph: [https://api.petstore.example.com/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available\&limit=100\&offset=0\&sort=name\&order=ascending\&include=category,tags,photoUrls](https://api.petstore.example.com/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available\&limit=100\&offset=0\&sort=name\&order=ascending\&include=category,tags,photoUrls)

A very long single word: Donaudampfschifffahrtselektrizitaetenhauptbetriebswerkbauunterbeamtengesellschaft

## Emphasis and links [#emphasis-and-links]

A paragraph with **bold text**, *italic text*, ***both at once***, `inline code`,
~~strikethrough~~, and [a link to the SDKs page](/sdks) beside [an external link](https://swagger.io).

***

A horizontal rule sits above this paragraph.

Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key. Send the same key with a retried request and the API returns the original response rather than performing the operation twice. Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours, which is long enough to cover a retry queue draining after an outage but short enough that keys can be recycled.


# Autolinks (/gfm/autolinks)



GFM turns bare URLs into links without any angle brackets or link syntax.

## Extended autolinks [#extended-autolinks]

A bare https URL: [https://swagger.io/specification/](https://swagger.io/specification/)

A bare http URL: [http://example.com/docs](http://example.com/docs)

A www autolink with no scheme: [www.example.com/petstore](http://www.example.com/petstore)

An email address: [support@example.com](mailto:support@example.com)

## Autolinks inside other text [#autolinks-inside-other-text]

See [https://swagger.io](https://swagger.io) for the specification, or write to [support@example.com](mailto:support@example.com) if that does not help.

A URL in parentheses ([https://example.com/a](https://example.com/a)) and one followed by a comma [https://example.com/b](https://example.com/b), then more text.

## Trailing punctuation [#trailing-punctuation]

GFM trims trailing punctuation from an autolink. Visit [https://example.com/page](https://example.com/page). And [https://example.com/other](https://example.com/other)!

## Classic autolinks [#classic-autolinks]

The pointy-bracket form: [https://swagger.io](https://swagger.io) and [support@example.com](mailto:support@example.com)

## Not autolinks [#not-autolinks]

Inside a code span: `https://example.com/not-a-link`

A bare domain with no www and no scheme: example.com/petstore

# Task lists (/gfm/task-lists)



GFM adds task list items to ordinary lists. Each should render as a checkbox.

## A flat list [#a-flat-list]

* [ ] An unchecked item
* [x] A checked item
* [x] A checked item with a capital X
* An ordinary item with no checkbox, in the same list

## Nested task lists [#nested-task-lists]

* [ ] Parent task
  * [x] Finished subtask
  * [ ] Unfinished subtask
    * [x] Deeper still
* [x] Second parent

## Ordered task list [#ordered-task-list]

1. [ ] First step
2. [x] Second step
3. [ ] Third step

## Task items carrying other content [#task-items-carrying-other-content]

* [ ] A task whose text has **bold**, `code` and [a link](/sdks)
* [x] A task with a following paragraph

  This paragraph belongs to the checked item above.


# Text formatting (/gfm/text-formatting)

## Emphasis edge cases [#emphasis-edge-cases]

*single asterisk* and *single underscore*

**double asterisk** and **double underscore**

***triple*** and ***triple underscore***

Intra-word emphasis: un*frigging*believable, and snake_case_word should NOT be emphasised.

Escaped characters: \*not emphasis\*, \_not emphasis\_, \`not code\`, # not a heading

A line ending with two spaces\
breaks here.

A line ending with a backslash\
breaks here too.

Simple `code`, with backticks `` ` `` inside, and ``a span with a `nested` backtick``.

# Authentication (/guides/authentication)



Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.

A sibling page at depth 1, reached at `/guides/authentication`.

## Detail [#detail]

Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key. Send the same key with a retried request and the API returns the original response rather than performing the operation twice. Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours, which is long enough to cover a retry queue draining after an outage but short enough that keys can be recycled.

| Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
| `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
| `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |

```python
import os
from petstore_sdk import SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiException

client = SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(api_key=os.environ["PETSTORE_API_KEY"])

def list_available_pets(limit: int = 100):
    try:
        return client.pet.find_pets_by_status(status="available", limit=limit)
    except ApiException as exc:
        if exc.status_code == 429:
            raise RuntimeError("rate limited; let the SDK retry policy handle this") from exc
        raise
```

## Notes [#notes]

1. Create an API key in the dashboard and store it outside your source tree.
2. Install the SDK for your language from its public registry.
   * TypeScript from npm
   * Python from PyPI
   * C# from NuGet
3. Construct one client and reuse it for the lifetime of your process.
   * The client owns a connection pool
   * Constructing one per request exhausts sockets under load
     * On Linux you will see `EADDRNOTAVAIL` first
     * On Windows the symptom is a slow creep in handle count
4. Make your first call against a read-only endpoint to confirm credentials.
5. Add error handling for `429` and `5xx` before you go to production.


# Guides (/guides)



Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.

This page sits **1 level** below the content root, at `/guides`.

## What this level covers [#what-this-level-covers]

Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.

| Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
| `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
| `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |

## Worked example [#worked-example]

```ts
import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
  try {
    const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
      const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
      return listAvailablePets(limit);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Checklist [#checklist]

1. Create an API key in the dashboard and store it outside your source tree.
2. Install the SDK for your language from its public registry.
   * TypeScript from npm
   * Python from PyPI
   * C# from NuGet
3. Construct one client and reuse it for the lifetime of your process.
   * The client owns a connection pool
   * Constructing one per request exhausts sockets under load
     * On Linux you will see `EADDRNOTAVAIL` first
     * On Windows the symptom is a slow creep in handle count
4. Make your first call against a read-only endpoint to confirm credentials.
5. Add error handling for `429` and `5xx` before you go to production.

> Pets created through the API are visible to every user in your organisation
> immediately. There is no draft state, and no soft delete: a `DELETE` removes
> the record and its photo attachments in the same transaction.

   * TypeScript from npm
   * Python from PyPI
   * C# from NuGet
3. Construct one client and reuse it for the lifetime of your process.
   * The client owns a connection pool
   * Constructing one per request exhausts sockets under load
     * On Linux you will see `EADDRNOTAVAIL` first
     * On Windows the symptom is a slow creep in handle count
4. Make your first call against a read-only endpoint to confirm credentials.
5. Add error handling for `429` and `5xx` before you go to production.


# Backoff (/guides/webhooks/delivery/retries/backoff)



Requests are rate limited per API key rather than per IP address. When you exceed the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` and sets `Retry-After` to the number of seconds remaining in the current window. The generated SDKs read that header and back off for you, so you only need to handle it directly if you are calling the API without an SDK.

This page sits **5 levels** below the content root, at `/guides/webhooks/delivery/retries/backoff`.

## What this level covers [#what-this-level-covers]

Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.

| Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
| `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
| `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |

## Worked example [#worked-example]

```ts
import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
  try {
    const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
      const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
      return listAvailablePets(limit);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Checklist [#checklist]

1. Create an API key in the dashboard and store it outside your source tree.
2. Install the SDK for your language from its public registry.
   * TypeScript from npm
   * Python from PyPI
   * C# from NuGet
3. Construct one client and reuse it for the lifetime of your process.
   * The client owns a connection pool
   * Constructing one per request exhausts sockets under load
     * On Linux you will see `EADDRNOTAVAIL` first
     * On Windows the symptom is a slow creep in handle count
4. Make your first call against a read-only endpoint to confirm credentials.
5. Add error handling for `429` and `5xx` before you go to production.

> Pets created through the API are visible to every user in your organisation
> immediately. There is no draft state, and no soft delete: a `DELETE` removes
> the record and its photo attachments in the same transaction.

# Jitter (/guides/webhooks/delivery/retries/backoff/jitter)



Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.

This page sits **6 levels** below the content root, at `/guides/webhooks/delivery/retries/backoff/jitter`.

## What this level covers [#what-this-level-covers]

Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key. Send the same key with a retried request and the API returns the original response rather than performing the operation twice. Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours, which is long enough to cover a retry queue draining after an outage but short enough that keys can be recycled.

| Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
| `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
| `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |

## Worked example [#worked-example]

```ts

      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
      return listAvailablePets(limit);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
| `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
| `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |

## Worked example [#worked-example]

```ts
import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiError } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({ apiKey: process.env.PETSTORE_API_KEY });

export async function listAvailablePets(limit = 100): Promise<Pet[]> {
  try {
    const { result } = await client.petController.findPetsByStatus({ status: "available", limit });
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ApiError && error.statusCode === 429) {
      const retryAfterSeconds = Number(error.headers["retry-after"] ?? 1);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, retryAfterSeconds * 1000));
      return listAvailablePets(limit);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Checklist [#checklist]

1. Create an API key in the dashboard and store it outside your source tree.
2. Install the SDK for your language from its public registry.
   * TypeScript from npm
   * Python from PyPI
   * C# from NuGet
3. Construct one client and reuse it for the lifetime of your process.
   * The client owns a connection pool
   * Constructing one per request exhausts sockets under load
     * On Linux you will see `EADDRNOTAVAIL` first
     * On Windows the symptom is a slow creep in handle count
4. Make your first call against a read-only endpoint to confirm credentials.
5. Add error handling for `429` and `5xx` before you go to production.

> Pets created through the API are visible to every user in your organisation
> immediately. There is no draft state, and no soft delete: a `DELETE` removes
> the record and its photo attachments in the same transaction.


# Signatures (/guides/webhooks/signatures)



Errors carry a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `message`. Match on `code` in your own error handling: the `message` is written for a developer reading a log and may be reworded between releases, while `code` is part of the contract and changes only with a major version bump.

A sibling page at depth 2, reached at `/guides/webhooks/signatures`.

## Detail [#detail]

The Petstore API exposes pets, store orders and user accounts over HTTPS. Every request is authenticated, every response is JSON, and every list endpoint is paginated. This page walks through the parts of that contract you are most likely to need on your first integration, and points at the reference pages for the rest.

| Endpoint            | Method | Auth    | Rate limit | Idempotent | Paginated | Typical latency | Introduced | Deprecated |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `/pet`              | POST   | API key | 100/min    | Yes        | No        | 45 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/{petId}`      | GET    | API key | 600/min    | Yes        | No        | 18 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByStatus` | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 120 ms          | v3.0       | —          |
| `/pet/findByTags`   | GET    | API key | 300/min    | Yes        | Yes       | 180 ms          | v3.0       | v3.2       |
| `/store/order`      | POST   | OAuth 2 | 60/min     | Yes        | No        | 90 ms           | v3.0       | —          |
| `/store/inventory`  | GET    | API key | 30/min     | Yes        | No        | 240 ms          | v3.1       | —          |
| `/user/login`       | GET    | None    | 10/min     | No         | No        | 60 ms           | v3.0       | v3.3       |

```python
import os
from petstore_sdk import SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client, ApiException

client = SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(api_key=os.environ["PETSTORE_API_KEY"])

def list_available_pets(limit: int = 100):
    try:
        return client.pet.find_pets_by_status(status="available", limit=limit)
    except ApiException as exc:
        if exc.status_code == 429:
            raise RuntimeError("rate limited; let the SDK retry policy handle this") from exc
        raise
```

## Notes [#notes]

1. Create an API key in the dashboard and store it outside your source tree.
2. Install the SDK for your language from its public registry.
   * TypeScript from npm
   * Python from PyPI
   * C# from NuGet
3. Construct one client and reuse it for the lifetime of your process.
   * The client owns a connection pool
   * Constructing one per request exhausts sockets under load
     * On Linux you will see `EADDRNOTAVAIL` first
     * On Windows the symptom is a slow creep in handle count
4. Make your first call against a read-only endpoint to confirm credentials.
5. Add error handling for `429` and `5xx` before you go to production.

type Player = {
  /**
   * The player name
   * ```php
   * $a = "60"
   * ```
   *
   * @default 'user'
   */
  name: string;
};

/**
 * A custom function.
 *
 * @example
 *
 * ```ts
 * const str = fn("hello world")
 * console.log(str)
 * ```
 */
function fn<const T extends string>(s: T): T {
  return s;
}

// ---cut---

console.g;

const player: Player = { name: 'Hello World' };

# Context Plugin (/context-plugin)

The context plugin teaches your AI coding assistant how to use this API's SDKs, so the code it writes for you calls the API the way the SDKs are meant to be used.

## Install [#install]

```bash
npx context-plugins install "/__downloads/plugin.zip"
```

## What it does [#what-it-does]

Once the plugin is installed, describe what you want to build and your assistant works from the SDK for your language: how to install it and create a client, how to authenticate, and which methods and types to use for each call. You spend less time correcting code written from guesses about the API.

## Supported languages [#supported-languages]

- TypeScript

- Python

- C#

## Supported platforms [#supported-platforms]

- Claude Code
- Cursor
- GitHub Copilot

# C# SDK (/sdks/csharp)

[Download SDK](/__downloads/sdk/csharp.zip) · [View source](https://github.com/acme/petstore-csharp) · [View on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Acme.Petstore.Sdk)

## Intro [#intro]

The Swagger Petstore - OpenAPI 3.0 SDK provides access to the [Swagger Petstore - OpenAPI 3.0 REST APIs](https://swagger.io).

This is a sample Pet Store Server based on the OpenAPI 3.0 specification.  You can find out more about
Swagger at [https://swagger.io](https://swagger.io). In the third iteration of the pet store, we've switched to the design first approach!
You can now help us improve the API whether it's by making changes to the definition itself or to the code.
That way, with time, we can improve the API in general, and expose some of the new features in OAS3.

Some useful links:

* [The Pet Store repository](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-petstore)
* [The source API definition for the Pet Store](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-petstore/blob/master/src/main/resources/openapi.yaml)

## Installation [#installation]

To add the SDK to your project from NuGet:

```bash
dotnet add package Acme.Petstore.Sdk
```

To build against the SDK source instead, add it as a project reference into your solution:

```bash
dotnet add reference <path-to-sdk>/SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30.csproj
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

### Dependency Injection [#dependency-injection]

Register the client with `IServiceCollection` and resolve it from the container. The `HttpClient` is managed by `IHttpClientFactory`. Configure the client's behavior through `SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30ClientOptions`.

```csharp
services.AddSwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(options =>
{
    options.PetstoreAuth = "YOUR_API_KEY";
    options.ApiKey = "YOUR_API_KEY";
    options.Environment = ServerEnvironment.Production;
    // TODO: configure more client options here
});
```

### Direct Instantiation [#direct-instantiation]

Create the client by passing an `HttpClient` you manage yourself. Configure the client's behavior through `SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30ClientOptions`.

```csharp
var httpClient = new HttpClient();
// TODO: configure more client options here
var options = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30ClientOptions
{
    PetstoreAuth = "YOUR_API_KEY",
    ApiKey = "YOUR_API_KEY",
    Environment = ServerEnvironment.Production,
};
var client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(httpClient, options);
```

## Intro [#intro]

The Swagger Petstore - OpenAPI 3.0 SDK provides access to the [Swagger Petstore - OpenAPI 3.0 REST APIs](https://swagger.io).

This is a sample Pet Store Server based on the OpenAPI 3.0 specification.  You can find out more about
Swagger at [https://swagger.io](https://swagger.io). In the third iteration of the pet store, we've switched to the design first approach!

Some useful links:

* [The Pet Store repository](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-petstore)

## Installation [#installation]

To install the SDK from PyPI, with whichever package manager your project uses:

```bash
pip install acme-petstore-sdk
```

```bash
uv add acme-petstore-sdk
```

```bash
poetry add acme-petstore-sdk
```

To install from the SDK source instead, give the tool a path containing a slash — a bare folder name is looked up on PyPI, and resolves to whatever project holds that name there:

```bash
pip install <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

### Synchronous client [#synchronous-client]

Construct `SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client` with keyword arguments, and call `close()` when you are done. Every argument is optional.

```python
from swagger_petstore_open_api_3_0 import SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client

client = SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(petstore_auth="YOUR_API_KEY", api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")

client.close()
```

Alternatively, scope it — `with SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

### Asynchronous client [#asynchronous-client]

`AsyncSwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client` mirrors `SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client` with **identical method names**, and every endpoint method is a coroutine. It takes the same arguments, with some differences — for example, the transport argument is `custom_async_http_client`.

```python
from asyncio import run

from swagger_petstore_open_api_3_0 import AsyncSwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncSwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(petstore_auth="YOUR_API_KEY", api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
    await client.aclose()

run(main())
```

Alternatively, scope it — `async with AsyncSwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

# TypeScript SDK (/sdks/typescript)

[Download SDK](/__downloads/sdk/typescript.zip) · [View source](https://github.com/acme/petstore-typescript) · [View on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@acme/petstore-sdk)

## Intro [#intro]

The Swagger Petstore - OpenAPI 3.0 SDK provides access to the [Swagger Petstore - OpenAPI 3.0 REST APIs](https://swagger.io).

This is a sample Pet Store Server based on the OpenAPI 3.0 specification.  You can find out more about
Swagger at [https://swagger.io](https://swagger.io). In the third iteration of the pet store, we've switched to the design first approach!
You can now help us improve the API whether it's by making changes to the definition itself or to the code.
That way, with time, we can improve the API in general, and expose some of the new features in OAS3.

Some useful links:

* [The Pet Store repository](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-petstore)
* [The source API definition for the Pet Store](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-petstore/blob/master/src/main/resources/openapi.yaml)

## Installation [#installation]

To add the SDK to your project from npm:

```bash
npm install @acme/petstore-sdk
```

To install from the SDK source instead, compile it to `dist/` — run its `build` script once in the SDK folder — then add it to your project by path:

```bash
npm install <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

Create one client and reuse it. Configure its behaviour through `ClientOptions`.

```ts
import { SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client } from "@acme/petstore-sdk";

const client = new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({
  petstoreAuth: "YOUR_API_KEY",
  apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
});
```

Nothing in `ClientOptions` is required — `new SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client()` compiles — and each option left out falls back to its default. This API declares one environment, so there is no environment to select and no host to state at the construction site.

### From CommonJS [#from-commonjs]

The package ships both dialects from a single entry, so `require` works with full types. In a TypeScript CommonJS file use the `import ... = require(...)` form — a plain destructuring `require` runs fine but gives you `any`.

```ts
import sdk = require("@acme/petstore-sdk");

const client = new sdk.SwaggerPetstoreOpenApi30Client({
  petstoreAuth: "YOUR_API_KEY",
  apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
});
```

# Add a new pet to the store. (/api/petstore/pet/addPet)

`POST /pet`

Add a new pet to the store.

# Update an existing pet. (/api/petstore/pet/updatePet)

`PUT /pet`

Update an existing pet by Id.

# Finds Pets by status. (/api/petstore/pet/findPetsByStatus)

`GET /pet/findByStatus`

Multiple status values can be provided with comma separated strings.

# Finds Pets by tags. (/api/petstore/pet/findPetsByTags)

`GET /pet/findByTags`

Multiple tags can be provided with comma separated strings. Use tag1, tag2, tag3 for testing.

# Find pet by ID. (/api/petstore/pet/getPetById)

`GET /pet/{petId}`

Returns a single pet.

# Updates a pet in the store with form data. (/api/petstore/pet/updatePetWithForm)

`POST /pet/{petId}`

Updates a pet resource based on the form data.

# Deletes a pet. (/api/petstore/pet/deletePet)

`DELETE /pet/{petId}`

Delete a pet.

# Uploads an image. (/api/petstore/pet/uploadFile)

`POST /pet/{petId}/uploadImage`

Upload image of the pet.

# Returns pet inventories by status. (/api/petstore/store/getInventory)

`GET /store/inventory`

Returns a map of status codes to quantities.

# Place an order for a pet. (/api/petstore/store/placeOrder)

`POST /store/order`

Place a new order in the store.

# Find purchase order by ID. (/api/petstore/store/getOrderById)

`GET /store/order/{orderId}`

For valid response try integer IDs with value <= 5 or > 10. Other values will generate exceptions.

# Delete purchase order by identifier. (/api/petstore/store/deleteOrder)

`DELETE /store/order/{orderId}`

For valid response try integer IDs with value < 1000. Anything above 1000 or non-integers will generate API errors.

# Create user. (/api/petstore/user/createUser)

`POST /user`

This can only be done by the logged in user.

# Creates list of users with given input array. (/api/petstore/user/createUsersWithListInput)

`POST /user/createWithList`

Creates list of users with given input array.

# Logs user into the system. (/api/petstore/user/loginUser)

`GET /user/login`

Log into the system.

# Logs out current logged in user session. (/api/petstore/user/logoutUser)

`GET /user/logout`

Log user out of the system.

# Get user by user name. (/api/petstore/user/getUserByName)

`GET /user/{usersname}`

Get user detail based on username.

# Delete user resource. (/api/petstore/user/deleteUser)

`DELETE /user/{usersname}`

This can only be done by the logged in user.

# Update user resource. (/api/petstore/user/updateUser)

`PUT /user/{usersname}`

This can only be done by the logged in user.
